title: Answer to an Old Name
story:
From: Tomasz Wierzba
Subject: The archive has moved, the scripts have not

Every 2019 field script fetches `http://archive/`. That machine no longer exists. Amara's replacement is called `archive-v2`, and I will not edit forty scripts by hand: one typo and a season of readings lands in the wrong place.

The network `legacy-net` already exists and `old-script` is running on it, still asking for the old name. Start `archive-v2` on that network so that the name `archive` reaches it. Confirm before the evening shift. I would like to sleep.
objectives: From inside `old-script`, `http://archive/` must return the archive's web page
startingState: Network `legacy-net` exists and container `old-script` (alpine) is running on it. Nothing answers to `archive` yet.
hints: A container can carry extra DNS names on a network besides its own name. Check the options of `docker run` that mention the network.
Use `--network legacy-net` together with `--network-alias <name>`. The alias only exists on the network it was given for.

```bash
docker run -d --name archive-v2 \
  --network legacy-net --network-alias archive \
  nginx:alpine
docker exec old-script wget -qO- http://archive/
```

commands: docker run -d --name old-script --network legacy-net alpine:3.20 sleep infinity

validation.description: `old-script` can fetch `http://archive/` and gets the nginx page

solution: docker run -d --name archive-v2 --network legacy-net --network-alias archive nginx:alpine
debrief: Old scripts keep working because the new container answers to the old hostname, and nobody had to touch a single client. Pro tip: aliases belong to one network, so the same container can go by different names on different networks.
